gate_b_decision.author: Antigravity Remote Sensing & Scientific Validation Engine
gate_b_decision.core_question: Are the harmonised data more comparable than the raw MODIS and VIIRS data?
gate_b_decision.core_finding: YES for the genuine sensor overlap era (2012–2026) and typical fire regimes (M <= 5), where harmonisation reduces the artificial Jan 2012 seam jump from +1,373.9% to +25.0% and maintains high seasonal correlation (r = 0.933) and peak-month preservation. HOWEVER, Gate B is awarded as a CONDITIONAL PASS because three structural limitations failed: (1) The pre-2002 Terra-only era lacks a diurnal bridge; (2) Extreme forest cell-weeks (M > 10) trigger unconstrained power-law extrapolation; (3) Active-fire uncertainty intervals achieve only 54.64% empirical coverage at nominal 80%.

authorized_for_release: Post-2012 overlap harmonised counts and FRP (weekly and monthly)
2002–2011 dual-MODIS typical fire weeks (with prediction tag)
restricted_or_flagged: Forest cell-weeks with M > 10 (labelled EXTRAPOLATION OUTLIER)
Active-fire uncertainty intervals (must display undercoverage warning)
Daily estimates (must display disaggregated weekly estimate tag)

gate_b_decision.next_milestone_readiness: APPROVED FOR MILESTONE M6 (Analysis Engine & Anomaly Detection)

test_inventory.question: Do the sensors keep a consistent relationship?
test_inventory.design: Fit on 2012–2018; check annual comparability across 2012–2026 overlap years
test_inventory.pass_rule: Yearly ratio or slope inside the bootstrap interval
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: Harmonisation achieves consistent order-of-magnitude comparability across all 15 overlap years.

test_inventory.question: Is the seasonal profile preserved?
test_inventory.design: Monthly profile of predicted versus observed VIIRS across calendar months 1–12
test_inventory.pass_rule: Pearson r >= 0.85, Spearman rho >= 0.85, peak-month agreement delta = 0
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Pearson r = 0.933, Spearman rho = 0.986, Peak month = March (delta = 0)
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: High linear and rank correlation; peak fire month perfectly preserved.

test_inventory.question: Does it work across ecosystems?
test_inventory.design: Error reported per agro-ecological class on held-out test data
test_inventory.pass_rule: No class hidden; poor classes flagged in the app
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Croplands (Delta & Inland), Shrubland, Urban pass (ratio 1.02–1.27x); Forest & Woodland shows power-law runaway during large fires
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: 4 of 5 classes pass cleanly. Forest & Woodland requires explicit flagging in app due to power-law runaway when M > 10.

test_inventory.question: Does it work in unseen places?
test_inventory.design: Pure spatial holdout excluding Cauvery Delta (Block 3) and Western Ghats (Block 4) across all training years
test_inventory.pass_rule: Held-out error within agreed margin of fitted error
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Cauvery Delta MAE = 0.544 (Test); Western Ghats MAE = 7.489 due to omitted montane forest samples
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: Cauvery Delta transfers cleanly. Western Ghats requires montane forest representation in training.

test_inventory.question: Does it hold in later years?
test_inventory.pass_rule: Held-out test error within 1.5x of validation error
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Test MAE = 2.038 vs Validation MAE = 1.536 (ratio = 1.327x <= 1.5x margin)
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: Held-out out-of-sample generalisation holds within pre-registered tolerance.

test_inventory.question: Are artificial jumps reduced?
test_inventory.design: Level-shift test across 12-month windows at Jan 2012, July 2002, May 2018, March 2023
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Jan 2012 jump reduced from +1373.9% to +25.0% (PASS). July 2002 jump +118.6% vs raw +79.8% (FAIL).
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: Jan 2012 MODIS-to-VIIRS seam successfully bridged. Pre-2002 Terra-only era uncalibrated without diurnal bridge.

test_inventory.question: Does it show where it is unreliable?
test_inventory.design: Coverage of 80% and 95% bootstrap intervals evaluated on held-out test data
test_inventory.pass_rule: Coverage near nominal; active-fire coverage honestly reported
test_inventory.quantitative_result: Overall 80% cov = 94.33%, 95% cov = 96.97% (PASS). Active-fire (V >= 1) cov = 54.64% (80%) and 75.69% (95%) (FAIL)
test_inventory.verdict_rationale: Marginal coverage meets nominal bounds due to zero-fire dominance, but active fires are under-covered. Calibrated claim rejected for active fires.

app_readiness_matrix.user_facing_caveat: Daily estimates represent weekly expectation allocated by satellite overpass; do not treat as independent daily ignitions.
Model-predicted VIIRS-equivalent. Validated for typical fire loads; not direct observations.
Lacks diurnal bridge for absent afternoon Aqua overpass. Substantially underestimates fire count. Excluded from automated trend analysis.

app_readiness_matrix.output_stream: Mega-Fire Forest Cell-Weeks (M > 10 in Forest & Woodland)
app_readiness_matrix.user_facing_caveat: Log-linear interaction exponent (3.903) produces unphysical counts during mega-fires. Robust median metrics must be used.
Intervals achieve nominal coverage marginally but capture only 54.6% of active fires due to MODIS omission. Do not interpret as calibrated for active events.
Model B improves median absolute error (17.0 MW vs 18.8 MW) but has higher linear MAE than raw MODIS due to mega-fire outlier skewness.
